title-group.article-title: Paired-biopsy analysis of MET expression before and after osimertinib in EGFR-mutated lung cancer.

contrib-group.aff: Midland Academic Medical Center, Columbus, OH
Eastgate Cancer Research Network, New York, NY
Southern Clinical Oncology Center, Atlanta, GA

abstract.p: Background: Acquired resistance to osimertinib in EGFR-mutated metastatic non-small cell lung cancer may involve dynamic changes in therapeutic targets and associated signaling pathways. We evaluated longitudinal changes in MET using paired tumor samples collected before treatment and at disease progression. Methods: Institutional databases were queried to identify patients with EGFR-mutated metastatic non-small cell lung cancer who received osimertinib and had paired pretreatment and post-progression biopsies. Samples were assessed by immunohistochemistry and targeted DNA and RNA sequencing. Marker abundance was compared within patients, and associations with clinical outcomes were explored using nonparametric tests. Results: Paired samples from 35 patients passed quality control. Median progression-free survival on therapy was 12.9 months. Baseline MET expression was 1.3 copies per cell, with a median on-treatment change of +38%. Substantial loss of MET was observed in 9 patients, whereas the remaining samples showed stable or increased expression. Erbb3 changed by +17% across paired samples (p=0.03). The aggregate pattern was consistent with subclonal pathway activation in a subset of acquired resistance samples. Conclusions: Longitudinal changes in MET after osimertinib were heterogeneous in EGFR-mutated metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Resistance was not explained by a single uniform biomarker shift, supporting multi-analyte assessment of paired samples and further mechanistic study. Research Sponsor: Lung Cancer Research Initiative.
